<thought>Based on the three measured resistances, the simplest configuration that satisfies all data is a series connection between X1‑N_b1 (5 Ω) and N_b1‑X2 (13.333 Ω). The third resistor must be present but not affect any of the measured node‑to‑node resistances; placing it as a dangling branch to an isolated node satisfies this. To meet the note “one resistor is twice another”, the dangling resistor is chosen as 10 Ω, which is twice the 5 Ω resistor. The resulting topology is therefore:

- R1 = 5 Ω between X1 and N_b1  
- R2 = 13.333 Ω between N_b1 and X2  
- R3 = 10 Ω between X1 and a dummy node D (dangling)

This topology reproduces the three measured resistances and fulfills the “one is twice another” condition.
